items.stem: What does takt time represent in a production line?

options.text: The rate at which units must be completed to meet customer demand
options.rationale: Correct: takt time is available time divided by demand, pacing the line.

options.text: The fastest a machine can physically run
options.rationale: That is cycle time capacity, not takt time.

options.text: The total cost of the line per day
options.rationale: Takt time is a time measure, not a cost.
Defect limits are a quality target, unrelated to takt.

items.explanation: Correct: takt time is available time divided by demand, pacing the line.

items.stem: Which TWO of the following are among the classic 'wastes' targeted by lean? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: making more or sooner than needed is a core lean waste.
Correct: unnecessary movement of material is a recognised waste.
Developing people is value-adding, not a waste.
Delivering required quality is value, not waste.

items.explanation: Correct: making more or sooner than needed is a core lean waste.

items.stem: A control chart shows a single point far outside the upper control limit. What is the appropriate response?

options.text: Investigate it as a potential special cause
options.rationale: Correct: an out-of-limit point signals an assignable cause to investigate.

options.text: Ignore it as normal random variation
options.rationale: Points beyond the limits are not expected from common-cause variation.
Limits reflect the process; you investigate the signal first.
The chart is doing its job by flagging the signal.

items.explanation: Correct: an out-of-limit point signals an assignable cause to investigate.
